title: Attention Is All You Need
authors_venue_year: Ashish Vaswani et al. (Google Brain & Google Research), NeurIPS 2017
core_breakthrough: Replaces recurrent and convolutional sequence models entirely with multi-head self-attention, enabling massive parallelization during training and setting the foundation for modern LLMs.

sublayers.name: Token Embedding Lookup
sublayers.explanation: Converts input discrete token IDs into dense continuous vector representations of dimension d_model, scaled by the square root of the hidden dimension.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Maps integer token indices {0..V-1} into continuous vector space ℝ^512 and multiplies by sqrt(512)=22.62 to balance magnitude with positional encodings.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Memory-bound gather operation from GPU DRAM. High cache hit rate when batch sequences share subwords.
sublayers.failure_modes: Without sqrt(d_model) scaling, embedding values become negligible relative to PE sinusoidal amplitudes, degrading early training convergence.

sublayers.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
sublayers.explanation: Injects sequence position information into token embeddings using deterministic sine and cosine wave functions of varying frequencies, enabling the model to attend to relative positions.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Deterministic harmonic waves. Even indices use sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d)), odd use cos. Dot product PE(pos+k) · PE(pos) is a function of offset k alone, providing translation invariance.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Precomputed and pinned in GPU constant memory. Zero runtime FLOPs during inference via static lookup.
sublayers.failure_modes: Cannot extrapolate accurately beyond context horizons unseen during training without frequency rescaling (RoPE / YaRN).
sublayers.pytorch_code:
pe[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div_term)
pe[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div_term)
x = x + pe[:x.size(1)]

sublayers.name: Embedding Dropout & Summation
sublayers.explanation: Adds the positional encodings to the token embeddings element-wise and applies dropout regularization with probability P_drop = 0.1.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Randomly zeros out channels with probability P_drop=0.1, scaling surviving elements by 1/(1-0.1) = 1.11 to preserve expected activation energy.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Fused into the embedding addition kernel to eliminate redundant DRAM roundtrips.
sublayers.failure_modes: Overly high dropout rates (e.g. >0.2) cause representation collapse and disrupt positional signal alignment.

sublayers.name: Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA)
sublayers.explanation: Linearly projects input tokens into h separate Query, Key, and Value subspaces (d_k = d_v = d_model / h = 64), computes scaled dot-product attention in parallel, and projects concatenated head outputs.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Q=X W_Q, K=X W_K, V=X W_V -> Reshape to (B, h=8, L, d_k=64) -> Attention score S = Q K^T / 8 -> Softmax(S) -> Multiply by V -> Concat 8 heads -> Project through W_O.
sublayers.hardware_notes: FlashAttention fuses QK^T, Softmax, and SV in on-chip SRAM, cutting memory bandwidth from O(L^2) to O(L).
sublayers.failure_modes: Without 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling, for large d_k dot products grow large, pushing softmax into regions with vanishing gradients.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(self.d_k)
attn = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
out = torch.matmul(attn, v).transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(B, L, D)
out = self.w_o(out)

sublayers.name: Residual Connection & Post-LayerNorm 1
sublayers.explanation: Applies a residual connection around the attention sublayer followed by layer normalization: LayerNorm(z) = ((z - mu) / sqrt(sigma^2 + eps)) * gamma + beta.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Identity highway: z = X + Dropout(MHSA(X)). Normalization: LN(z) = ((z - μ) / sqrt(σ^2 + ε)) · γ + β computed across channel dimension d=512.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Pre-LayerNorm variant is preferred in modern transformers to stabilize gradients in deep stacks without warm-up heuristics.
sublayers.failure_modes: Post-LN can suffer from vanishing gradients at initialization for N > 12 layers unless strict learning rate warmup is enforced.

sublayers.name: Position-Wise Feed-Forward Network (FFN)
sublayers.explanation: Applies two linear transformations with an inner ReLU activation independently and identically to each sequence position, expanding dimension from d_model=512 to d_ff=2048.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Two-stage linear expansion: W_1 expands 512 -> 2048 (4x factor). ReLU introduces point-wise non-linearity. W_2 projects 2048 -> 512 back to model dimension.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Matrix multiplications GEMM 1 and GEMM 2 dominate parameter count (66% of total block parameters). High compute density on Tensor Cores.
sublayers.failure_modes: Dead ReLUs if learning rate is excessively high; modern models use SwiGLU / GeLU to mitigate dying neurons.

sublayers.name: Residual Connection & Post-LayerNorm 2
sublayers.explanation: Applies a second residual addition and layer normalization over the FFN sublayer to form the complete encoder block output.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Second residual bypass and LayerNorm step: X_out = LN(X_norm1 + Dropout(FFN(X_norm1))). Prepares representations for subsequent stack layer.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Fused Add+Norm CUDA kernel reduces global memory access latency.
sublayers.failure_modes: LayerNorm saturation if gamma scale parameters drift unchecked.

sublayers.name: Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention
sublayers.formula_katex: \text{MaskedAttention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\right)V, \quad M_{ij} = \begin{cases} 0 & j \le i \\ -\infty & j > i \end{cases}
sublayers.explanation: Calculates self-attention over target tokens with upper-triangular masking (-infinity) to enforce causality and prevent positions from attending to subsequent tokens.
sublayers.source_section: Section 3.2.3 (Applications of Attention in our Model)
sublayers.math_breakdown: Applies additive causal mask M where M_ij = -inf for j > i before softmax. Prevents position i from attending to future tokens j > i.
sublayers.hardware_notes: During inference, cached past keys/values (KV cache) avoid recomputing historical token projections: O(L) generation step.
sublayers.failure_modes: Causal mask leakage leads to training-inference discrepancy and autoregressive degradation.

sublayers.name: Encoder-Decoder Cross-Attention
sublayers.explanation: Generates Queries from the previous decoder sublayer and fetches Keys and Values from the final output representation of the encoder stack.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Queries projected from decoder stream, Keys and Values projected from encoder final stack output: CrossAttn = softmax(Q_dec K_enc^T / sqrt(d_k)) V_enc.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Encoder KV states are static throughout the entire decoding phase and computed once during prompt prefill.
sublayers.failure_modes: Attention dispersion over long source sequences; alignment collapse if encoder representations lack contrast.

sublayers.name: Decoder Position-Wise FFN & LayerNorm
sublayers.explanation: Executes identical position-wise feed-forward transformations with residual connections and layer normalization across each decoder layer.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Identical structure to encoder FFN: expands channel dimension by 4x to synthesize cross-lingual or next-token contextual features.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Standard high-throughput GEMM layer.
sublayers.failure_modes: Representation bottleneck if intermediate capacity d_ff is constrained below 4x.

sublayers.name: Vocabulary Linear Projection
sublayers.explanation: Projects the decoder final output representation from d_model dimensions to the full vocabulary size V (with weights tied to input embeddings).
sublayers.math_breakdown: Projects final hidden states through transpose of embedding matrix W_e^T (weight tying) to produce unnormalized logits across vocabulary.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Large matrix multiplication across vocabulary. Can be a latency bottleneck for V > 100,000 without split-K kernels.
sublayers.failure_modes: Logit drift without proper layer normalization preceding the projection head.

sublayers.name: Next-Token Softmax Classifier
sublayers.explanation: Converts unnormalized output logits into predictive probabilities over next target tokens.
sublayers.math_breakdown: P(y_t+1 = i | context) = exp(z_i) / sum_j exp(z_j). Computes calibrated conditional probability distribution over dictionary.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Fused CrossEntropyLoss in PyTorch computes log_softmax and NLL loss simultaneously in FP32 to avoid numerical underflow.
sublayers.failure_modes: Numerical overflow when max logit is large; fixed via subtraction of max(z) before exponentiation.

pros.claim: Full parallelization across entire sequence length during training without recurrence sequential bottlenecks.
O(1) maximum path length between any two arbitrary token positions in the sequence, enabling perfect direct dependency modeling.
Established state-of-the-art machine translation results (28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 En-De) at a fraction of previous training cost.

cons.claim: Quadratic computational complexity O(L^2 * d) in both FLOPs and memory with respect to sequence length L.
cons.source_section: Table 1 (Maximum path lengths and per-layer complexity)

cons.claim: KV Cache grows linearly with sequence length during autoregressive generation, causing severe GPU memory exhaustion at long contexts.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: Outperformed previous best ensemble model by >2.0 BLEU with 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs
Established single-model state-of-the-art outperforming all previous models

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
authors_venue_year: Albert Gu (Carnegie Mellon) & Tri Dao (Princeton), arXiv 2023
core_breakthrough: Introduces input-dependent selective state space models (S6) and a hardware-aware parallel prefix scan in GPU SRAM, achieving Transformer-quality language modeling with linear O(L) time and constant O(1) inference state size.

sublayers.name: Channel Dimension Linear Expansion
sublayers.explanation: Expands input dimension D by expansion factor (default expand=2) to dimension E=2D, doubling the channel capacity for internal representation.

sublayers.name: Dual-Branch Splitting
sublayers.formula_katex: x_{ssm}, z = \text{Split}(X_{expand}), \quad x_{ssm} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}, \; z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}
sublayers.explanation: Splits the expanded representation into two parallel pathways: the SSM sequence processing branch and the multiplicative gating branch.

sublayers.name: Depthwise Causal 1D Convolution
sublayers.explanation: Applies a short 1D depthwise convolution with kernel size 4 along the sequence dimension to mix local contextual tokens and prevent independent channel processing before SSM.

sublayers.name: Convolutional SiLU Activation
sublayers.explanation: Applies smooth non-linear Swish/SiLU activation function to the convolved features.

sublayers.name: Input-Dependent Delta Step Size
sublayers.explanation: Projects token representation dynamically to produce time-step parameter Delta_t, controlling how much the model focuses on or ignores the current input token.

sublayers.name: Input-Dependent State Matrices B and C
sublayers.formula_katex: B_t = \text{Linear}_N(x'_{ssm, t}), \quad C_t = \text{Linear}_N(x'_{ssm, t}), \quad B_t, C_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times N}
sublayers.explanation: Dynamically projects token features to state matrices B (input matrix) and C (output matrix) with state dimension N=16, enabling selective content-based memory writing and reading.

sublayers.name: HiPPO Transition Matrix Parameterization
sublayers.explanation: Initializes transition matrix A using High-Order Polynomial Projection Operators (HiPPO) and maintains negative real diagonal representation for stable state decay.

sublayers.name: Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) Discretization
sublayers.formula_katex: \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = (\Delta_t A)^{-1}(\exp(\Delta_t A) - I) \cdot (\Delta_t B_t) \approx \Delta_t B_t
sublayers.explanation: Converts continuous ODE state parameters (A, B) into discrete recurrent step matrices (A_bar, B_bar) dynamic at each sequence position t.

sublayers.name: Hardware-Aware SRAM Parallel Associative Scan
sublayers.formula_katex: h_t = \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x'_{ssm, t}, \quad y_t = C_t h_t
sublayers.explanation: Fuses discretization and prefix scan directly in fast GPU on-chip SRAM memory without materializing the large (B, L, D, N) state tensors in slow High Bandwidth Memory (HBM).

sublayers.name: SiLU Multiplicative Gating
sublayers.explanation: Multiplies the output of the selective SSM block element-wise with the SiLU-activated gating branch z.

sublayers.name: Output Linear Projection & Skip Residual
sublayers.formula_katex: y_{out} = y_{gated} W_{out} + x, \quad W_{out} \in \mathbb{R}^{E \times D}
sublayers.explanation: Projects the gated representation back to model dimension D and adds the input residual skip connection.

pros.claim: Linear O(L) time and memory complexity during training with sequence length, enabling 1M+ token contexts.
Constant O(1) inference state size per layer (D * N parameters) with zero KV cache memory growth during generation.
Solves synthetic Induction Heads and Selective Copying tasks with 100% accuracy, matching Transformer reasoning capacity.

cons.claim: Fixed-capacity hidden state bottleneck when storing complex multi-hop associative memories across millions of tokens compared to full non-compressed KV attention.
Requires specialized hardware-fused Triton/CUDA kernels to prevent memory bandwidth bottlenecks from large state sizes.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: Mamba achieves 100% accuracy while S4 and H3 fail (<20%) at sequence length 4096
Generalizes to sequence length 2^20 (1,048,576 tokens) with 100% accuracy
Matches and exceeds Pythia-1.4B (64.2%) and RWKV-1.5B (64.5%)

title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
authors_venue_year: David Raposo, Sam Ritter et al. (Google DeepMind), arXiv 2024
core_breakthrough: Dynamically routes tokens across model depth by enforcing a fixed per-block compute capacity budget (e.g. top-50% tokens), allowing unselected tokens to bypass layers via residual connections for 50% FLOP savings with no quality loss.

sublayers.name: Scalar Token Priority Scoring
sublayers.explanation: A learned linear router projection assigns a single scalar affinity weight r_i to each sequence token x_i denoting its requirement for layer computation.

sublayers.name: Router Gradient Multiplication Pathway
sublayers.explanation: Multiplies the block output f(x_i) by the router weight r_i so that gradients from task loss backpropagate directly into the router weights.

sublayers.name: Fixed Sequence Capacity Budgeting
sublayers.explanation: Enforces a strict static capacity budget C equal to a fraction c (e.g. c=0.5) of total sequence length T, ensuring predictable deterministic static tensor shapes on hardware.

sublayers.name: Top-K Token Selection
sublayers.explanation: Selects the C tokens with the highest router scalar scores to undergo compute inside the current layer.

sublayers.name: Tensor Gathering
sublayers.explanation: Compacts only the selected C tokens into a dense tensor of size (B, C, D) for hardware-accelerated batch execution.

sublayers.name: Sublayer Execution (Self-Attention or MLP)
sublayers.explanation: Executes standard Transformer self-attention or feed-forward operations exclusively on the compacted tensor.

sublayers.name: Scatter & Pure Residual Skip
sublayers.formula_katex: x_i^{(l+1)} = \begin{cases} x_i^{(l)} + r_i \cdot \tilde{h}_i & \text{if } i \in \mathcal{S} \\ x_i^{(l)} & \text{if } i \notin \mathcal{S} \end{cases}
sublayers.explanation: Scatters computed token updates back into the full sequence while unselected tokens bypass the block completely via identity residual skip.

sublayers.name: Auxiliary Routing Loss
sublayers.explanation: Optional auxiliary loss to stabilize router decisions when using learned routing thresholds rather than top-k selection.

sublayers.name: Compound MoD + MoE Hierarchical Routing
sublayers.explanation: Jointly routes tokens along depth (MoD) and width (MoE) to simultaneously optimize compute per token and parameter capacity.

pros.claim: Achieves identical or superior log-perplexity to vanilla Transformers while consuming 50% fewer FLOPs per forward pass.
Enables 2x faster step execution during autoregressive inference when skipping attention/MLP layers for unselected tokens.
Predictable static compute tensor shapes (B, C, D) avoid dynamic shape compilation overhead on TPUs/GPUs.

cons.claim: Tokens that skip attention layers cannot attend to surrounding tokens at that layer depth, potentially limiting multi-hop reasoning if under-allocated.
Top-k capacity selection introduces non-causal dependency across the sequence during training unless causal router masks are applied.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: MoD outperforms baseline Transformer at same training compute budget
Maintains baseline accuracy with half the compute FLOPs per token

nodes.description: Full sequence of T tokens.
nodes.undertones: Easy tokens and hard tokens enter with uniform representation.

nodes.label: Per-Token Router MLP (r_i)
nodes.description: Computes scalar compute affinity weight r_i = w_r^T x_i for every token.
nodes.undertones: Learns to predict which tokens benefit from extra depth vs tokens that can skip.

nodes.label: Top-K Capacity Filter (C = c · T)
nodes.description: Selects top-50% (or top-k) highest priority tokens to allocate FLOPs.
nodes.undertones: Guarantees deterministic, static tensor dimensions for zero hardware fragmentation.

nodes.label: Tensor Gather (B, C, D)
nodes.description: Packs selected tokens into compacted dense compute buffer.
nodes.undertones: Maximizes TPU/GPU matrix engine utilization without computing on dummy padding.

nodes.label: Self-Attention / MLP Block
nodes.description: Deep transformer computation applied strictly to the compacted tensor.
nodes.undertones: Executes 2x faster because attention matrix is (C x C) instead of (T x T).

nodes.label: Scatter + Pure Residual Skip
nodes.description: Scatters computed outputs back modulated by router weight; unselected tokens skip via identity.
nodes.undertones: Unselected tokens preserve original representation losslessly.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Mixture of Experts: Algorithms, Theory, and Applications
authors_venue_year: Siyuan Mu & Sen Lin, Survey Paper 2024
core_breakthrough: Provides a comprehensive architectural taxonomy of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, detailing gating algorithms, fine-grained/shared expert designs, load balancing losses, and distributed expert parallelism.

sublayers.name: Top-K Softmax Sparse Gating
sublayers.formula_katex: G(x)_i = \text{softmax}(\text{TopK}(W_g x + \epsilon, k))_i, \quad \text{TopK}(v, k)_i = \begin{cases} v_i & \text{if } v_i \in \text{top } k \\ -\infty & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
sublayers.explanation: Calculates routing probabilities and sparsely dispatches each token to only the top-k highest scoring expert networks (e.g. k=1 in Switch Transformer, k=2 in GShard/Mixtral).

sublayers.name: Expert Choice Routing (EC)
sublayers.formula_katex: S_{i, j} = (X W_g)_{i, j}, \quad \mathcal{T}_j = \text{TopK}(\{S_{i, j}\}_{i=1}^T, C_e)
sublayers.explanation: Inverts routing logic so that each expert selects its top C_e tokens, guaranteeing perfectly balanced workload across all experts and eliminating token dropping.

sublayers.name: DeepSeekMoE Fine-Grained & Shared Expert Architecture
sublayers.explanation: Splits standard experts into N fine-grained smaller experts and isolates N_s dedicated shared experts that are always activated to capture common knowledge.

sublayers.name: Soft MoE & Slot-Based Dispatch
sublayers.explanation: Passes soft continuous linear combinations of tokens into expert slots, achieving fully differentiable expert routing without discrete top-k selection.

sublayers.name: Feed-Forward Expert Subnetwork (SwiGLU / GeLU)
sublayers.explanation: Individual expert modules structured as independent feed-forward networks (FFNs), typically employing modern SwiGLU activations.

sublayers.name: Multi-Head Latent Experts (MHLE) & Hierarchical MoE
sublayers.explanation: Two-level hierarchical tree-based gating that first selects expert clusters, then routes to specific specialized experts within that cluster.

sublayers.name: Switch Load Balancing Auxiliary Loss
sublayers.formula_katex: \mathcal{L}_{aux} = \alpha \cdot N \sum_{i=1}^N f_i P_i, \quad f_i = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{I}(\text{argmax}(G(x_t))=i), \; P_i = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T G(x_t)_i
sublayers.explanation: Encourages uniform distribution of tokens across experts by penalizing the dot product between actual fraction of tokens dispatched f_i and average routing probability P_i.

sublayers.name: Router Z-Loss (Numerical Stability)
sublayers.explanation: Penalizes large router pre-softmax logits to prevent floating-point rounding errors and numerical instability during large-scale distributed training.

sublayers.name: All-to-All Token Dispatch & Combine Collectives
sublayers.explanation: Coordinates inter-GPU communication primitives: tokens on worker GPUs are dispatched across network interconnect to expert host GPUs and gathered back.

pros.claim: Decouples model parameter capacity from computational cost per token, enabling models with 10x-100x more parameters at constant FLOPs.
Fine-grained expert routing allows domain specialization where different experts master code, math, syntax, or knowledge subsets.

cons.claim: Heavy All-to-All inter-device communication overhead creates network bandwidth bottlenecks during distributed GPU training.
Susceptible to routing collapse (expert starvation/overload) and requires complex hyperparameter tuning of auxiliary balancing losses.

reported_metrics.source_section: Section V (Applications, Table summarizing MoE models)
reported_metrics.comparison_context: MoE models match dense model quality with 25% of active compute per token
Shared experts capture 90%+ common patterns while routed experts specialize

title: Sliding Window Attention Training for Efficient Large Language Models
authors_venue_year: Zichuan Fu et al. (Tencent YouTu & CityU HK), arXiv 2025
core_breakthrough: Proposes SWAT, an efficient pre-training framework that replaces Softmax with Sigmoid attention and unifies balanced ALiBi + RoPE embeddings to eliminate attention sinks and enable stable sliding window training on long contexts.

sublayers.name: Independent Sigmoid Attention Scoring
sublayers.explanation: Replaces the global softmax normalization across tokens with an element-wise independent Sigmoid activation, decoupling token score sums and preventing the attention sink phenomenon.

sublayers.name: Attention Sink Elimination
sublayers.explanation: Because each token score is computed independently without a denominator sum, initial tokens no longer receive disproportionate attention mass simply to soak up unused probability.

sublayers.name: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) for Local Context
sublayers.formula_katex: q'_m = R_{\Theta, m}^d q_m, \quad k'_n = R_{\Theta, n}^d k_n
sublayers.explanation: Applies rotary embedding to query and key vectors to encode high-precision relative positional information within the local sliding window.

sublayers.name: Balanced ALiBi Linear Decay Bias
sublayers.explanation: Adds a geometric negative linear bias to attention scores based on distance, stabilizing attention decay and preventing sharp boundary artifacts at sliding window edges.

sublayers.name: Multi-Scale Layer Receptive Field Expansion
sublayers.explanation: By stacking L layers each with sliding window size W, the effective receptive field grows linearly across network depth, achieving global sequence visibility at top layers.

layers.layer_name: Linear Cache Management & SWAT Inference Pipeline

sublayers.name: Constant-Size Sliding KV Ring-Buffer
sublayers.formula_katex: \text{Memory}_{KV} = 2 \cdot B \cdot W \cdot D \cdot N_{layers} = O(W \cdot D)
sublayers.explanation: Maintains a fixed-size ring buffer for Key and Value vectors of size W tokens, eliminating linear KV cache memory expansion during long-sequence generation.

pros.claim: Maintains constant memory footprint O(W * D) per layer regardless of sequence length N, preventing out-of-memory errors on long sequences.
Achieves training throughput improvements of 4x-8x over full attention when pre-training on sequences up to 32k tokens.
Sigmoid attention eliminates attention sink artifacts and prevents perplexity degradation when evaluating on extended sequence lengths.

cons.claim: Maximum single-layer direct attention distance is strictly bounded by window size W.
Requires careful tuning of ALiBi slope ratios m_h to prevent over-decaying long-range semantic information in early layers.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: SWAT matches Full-Attention baseline (77.4%) with 50% window size
Competitive with standard LLaMA-style dense attention (73.5%)
Exceeds Mistral-SWA baseline (46.8%) due to Sigmoid attention stabilization

nodes.label: Dual Positional Engine (RoPE + Balanced ALiBi)
nodes.description: Applies RoPE for local token precision and geometric ALiBi slope decay for boundary smoothness.
nodes.undertones: Prevents abrupt truncation artifacts at sliding window edges.

nodes.label: Independent Sigmoid Attention Scoring
nodes.description: Computes Sigmoid(QK^T / sqrt(d_k) + B) * V without softmax global normalization.
nodes.undertones: Completely eliminates Attention Sink artifacts where token 0 absorbs false probability.

nodes.label: Sliding Window KV Ring Buffer (Window W)
nodes.description: Maintains constant O(W x D) memory KV cache per layer during training & inference.
nodes.undertones: Prevents GPU memory cliffs on extended contexts.

nodes.label: Multi-Scale Layer Receptive Field Stacking
nodes.description: Cumulative receptive field expands linearly L x (W-1) + 1 to cover full sequence.
nodes.undertones: Deep layers receive global multi-hop context through intermediate layer bridges.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
authors_venue_year: Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong, Vahab Mirrokni (Google Research), arXiv 2024/2025
core_breakthrough: Introduces Neural Long-Term Memory (NMM) updated at test-time via gradient descent on an associative surprise loss with surprise momentum and data-dependent decay, coupled with short-term sliding window attention across MAC, MAG, and MAL architectures.

layers.layer_name: Associative Memory Loss & Surprise Gradient Engine

sublayers.name: Memory Key-Value Association Objective
sublayers.formula_katex: \mathcal{L}_{mem}(M_t; x_t) = \| M_t(k_t) - v_t \|_2^2, \quad k_t = x_t W_K, \; v_t = x_t W_V
sublayers.explanation: Defines associative memory reconstruction loss where neural memory network M_t is trained to predict value vector v_t given key vector k_t.

sublayers.name: Surprise Gradient Calculation
sublayers.explanation: Calculates the instantaneous surprise of an input token as the gradient of the memory loss with respect to the neural memory weights.

sublayers.name: Surprise Momentum Accumulator
sublayers.explanation: Maintains a momentum term S_t that acts as a temporal memory of surprise across sequence history, modulated by data-dependent learning rate theta_t and momentum decay eta_t.

sublayers.name: Memory Weight Update & Forgetting
sublayers.explanation: Updates the neural memory weights via generalized forgetting (weight decay alpha_t) and integrated surprise momentum S_t.

sublayers.name: Deep Multi-Layer Perceptron Memory
sublayers.explanation: Implements the memory as deep non-linear MLP weight matrices rather than static vector slots, massively increasing memory storage capacity.

sublayers.name: Parallel Chunked Training Algorithm
sublayers.explanation: Formulates mini-batch test-time gradient updates as associative parallel matrix multiplications for fast GPU hardware execution.

sublayers.name: MAC (Memory as Context) Topology
sublayers.explanation: Retrieves memory context tokens, concatenates them with task-level persistent memory prefix P and input tokens, and feeds them into short-term sliding window attention.

sublayers.name: MAG (Memory as Gate) Topology
sublayers.formula_katex: Y = g_t \odot Y_{\text{attn}} + (1 - g_t) \odot Y_{\text{mem}}, \quad g_t = \text{sigmoid}(\text{Linear}([Y_{\text{attn}}, Y_{\text{mem}}]))
sublayers.explanation: Processes input in parallel through short-term attention and neural memory, combining their outputs via a learned dynamic gate g_t.

sublayers.name: MAL (Memory as Layer) Topology
sublayers.explanation: Stacks neural memory layers sequentially with sliding-window attention layers as modular building blocks.

pros.claim: Can memorize and retrieve information across sequences of 2M+ tokens with linear computational scaling and fast inference.
Surprise-driven update prevents memory overflow by prioritizing memorable, unexpected tokens over redundant background text.
Test-time learning allows the model to continuously adapt and update its internal weights during generation without pre-training updates.

cons.claim: Test-time gradient computation requires backpropagation operations during the forward inference pass, adding computational overhead per token.
More complex mathematical formulation and implementation than standard linear attention models.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: Titans (MAC) significantly outperforms Mamba, RWKV, and Recurrent baselines (<50%)
Matches full attention Transformer while maintaining linear scaling

nodes.undertones: Handles immediate syntax and local dependencies while NMM handles distant history.

nodes.undertones: Configurable topology depending on downstream latency requirements.

title: TransMamba: A Sequence-Level Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
authors_venue_year: Yixing Li, Ruobing Xie et al. (Tencent Hunyuan & CUHK), AAAI 2026
core_breakthrough: Unifies Transformer and Mamba at the sequence level through shared parameter projection matrices (QKV <-> CBx) and Memory Compression Cache, dynamically switching between Attention and SSM at TransPoints.

sublayers.name: Unified Matrix Weight Sharing
sublayers.formula_katex: \begin{bmatrix} Q_t \\ K_t \\ V_t \end{bmatrix} \longleftrightarrow \begin{bmatrix} C_t \\ B_t \\ x_t \end{bmatrix} = x_t W_{proj}, \quad W_{proj} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times 3D}
sublayers.explanation: Shares a single parameter projection matrix W_proj to generate QKV for Transformer attention or CBx for Mamba SSM, enabling zero-parameter overhead switching.

sublayers.name: TransPoint Node Partitioning
sublayers.explanation: Calculates initial sequence tokens using full Transformer attention for rich prompt reasoning, then transitions at TransPoint threshold to linear Mamba2 SSM.

sublayers.name: Layer-Specific TransPoint Scheduling
sublayers.explanation: Assigns different TransPoints across layer depths (e.g. earlier layers transition sooner while deep reasoning layers retain longer attention spans).

sublayers.name: Lossless Attention-to-SSM State Transfer
sublayers.explanation: Converts historical Transformer KV cache and attention outputs into the initial continuous recurrent hidden state for downstream Mamba computation.

sublayers.name: Autoregressive Hybrid Decoder Block Stack
sublayers.explanation: Executes stacked hybrid decoder layers combining shared parameter transformations, SSM recurrence, and multi-task generalization capabilities.

pros.claim: Achieves up to 40% reduction in relative training time compared to vanilla Transformer at identical model size.
Zero parameter overhead from dual mechanisms due to shared QKV and CBx projection matrices.
Maintains superior in-context learning and multi-task reasoning capabilities where pure Mamba struggles.

cons.claim: Performance is sensitive to TransPoint scheduling strategy; sub-optimal transition points degrade in-context learning.
KV cache memory must still be maintained during the initial sequence portion before the TransPoint.

reported_metrics.comparison_context: Outperforms pure Mamba2 (58.4 F1) and matches Transformer (64.1 F1)
Significantly faster training with equivalent evaluation loss

nodes.label: Input Token Sequence [x_1, ..., x_T]
nodes.description: Token stream entering hybrid layer.
nodes.undertones: Prompt prefix requires high-precision reasoning; continuation requires fast throughput.

nodes.label: Unified Shared Projection Matrix (W_proj)
nodes.description: Single weight matrix shared between Transformer [Q, K, V] and Mamba [C, B, x].
nodes.undertones: Zero parameter overhead when switching between Attention and SSM.

nodes.label: Sequence TransPoint Scheduler (N_trans)
nodes.description: Routes first N_trans tokens to Transformer and subsequent tokens to Mamba2 SSM.
nodes.undertones: Dynamically tunes where attention ends and SSM begins across layer depths.

nodes.label: Transformer Attention Regime (t ≤ N_trans)
nodes.description: Executes full multi-head self-attention on prompt tokens for in-context learning.
nodes.undertones: Captures complex multi-needle prompts and associative prompts flawlessly.

nodes.label: Memory Compression Cache (MCC)
nodes.description: Compresses Transformer KV and attention representations into continuous SSM state h_ssm.
nodes.undertones: Seamless, lossless knowledge handover at the TransPoint boundary.

nodes.label: Mamba2 SSM Linear Scan Regime (t > N_trans)
nodes.description: Executes linear-time selective scan for fast long sequence continuation.
nodes.undertones: Achieves 40% training speedup with constant generation memory.

title: P100SuperCNN: An Efficient Deep Learning Model for Image Classification on Resource Constrained Environment
authors_venue_year: Debi Prasad Panda and Pratik Kiran Rout (Department of CSE & IT, GITA, Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
core_breakthrough: A bespoke parameter-efficient hierarchical CNN combining MBConvSD (Inverted Residuals + Stochastic Depth), Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) channel attention, and 3-stage progressive augmentation to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on CIFAR-100 with only 4.03M parameters (15.4 MB footprint, 26% higher parameter efficiency than EfficientNet-B0 and 66% smaller than ResNet-18).

sublayers.name: Standard 3x3 Convolution Stem
sublayers.explanation: Initial lightweight spatial feature extraction converting 3-channel RGB image (32x32x3) into 32 high-dimensional feature maps (32x32x32) with zero spatial resolution downsampling.
sublayers.math_breakdown: 3x3 kernel sliding across RGB channels: FLOPs = 2 * 3 * 32 * 32 * 32 * 3^2 = 1.77 MFLOPs. Captures low-level spatial edges and color textures.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Extremely memory efficient on microcontrollers; preserves full spatial resolution for fine-grained CIFAR-100 classification.
sublayers.failure_modes: Using stride=2 in stem causes aggressive early spatial loss on small 32x32 images, degrading classification accuracy.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
self.stem = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
    nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
)

sublayers.name: 1x1 Pointwise Expansion Conv
sublayers.formula_katex: X_{exp} = \text{Swish}(\text{BatchNorm}(\text{Conv1x1}(X_{in}, W_{exp}))) \quad (C \rightarrow t \cdot C, \; t=4 \text{ to } 6)
sublayers.explanation: Expands input channel dimension by expansion factor t into a higher-dimensional representation space before spatial filtering.
sublayers.source_section: Poster: Core Component - The MBConvSD Block
sublayers.math_breakdown: 1x1 linear matrix multiplication across channels. Inverts traditional bottleneck structure by expanding rather than compressing channels.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Compute-bound GEMM operation well optimized on mobile NPUs and edge DSPs.
sublayers.failure_modes: Excessive expansion factors (t > 8) blow up SRAM activation memory on edge microcontrollers.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
self.expand_conv = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(in_c, expanded_c, 1, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(expanded_c),
    nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
)

sublayers.name: 3x3 Depthwise Separable Convolution
sublayers.explanation: Applies a separate 3x3 spatial filter per expanded channel independently, decoupling spatial filtering from channel mixing.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Computes 1 filter per channel. Computation cost is only 1/C_out of standard convolution (8x-9x FLOPs reduction).
sublayers.hardware_notes: High arithmetic intensity when fused with BatchNorm and activation in hardware registers.
sublayers.failure_modes: Standard non-depthwise convolutions require 9x more FLOPs and exceed edge memory budgets.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
self.dw_conv = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(expanded_c, expanded_c, 3, stride=stride, padding=1, groups=expanded_c, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(expanded_c),
    nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
)

sublayers.name: Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) Attention
sublayers.explanation: Lightweight channel-wise attention mechanism: squeezes spatial feature maps into 1D channel descriptors via Global Average Pooling, then learns non-linear inter-channel dependencies via two FC layers with reduction ratio r=4.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Global pooling z_c = 1/(H*W) sum(X_{c,i,j}). Gating s = sigmoid(W2 * SiLU(W1 * z)). Recalibrates channel weights to amplify informative features and suppress noise.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Negligible FLOPs and parameter cost (<1.5% parameters) with significant accuracy boost on fine-grained classes.
sublayers.failure_modes: Setting reduction ratio r too high (e.g. r=16) loses inter-channel nuance; setting r=1 causes parameter bloat.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
z = x.mean((2, 3), keepdim=True)
s = torch.sigmoid(self.fc2(F.silu(self.fc1(z))))
x = x * s

sublayers.name: 1x1 Linear Pointwise Projection
sublayers.explanation: Projects expanded channel representations back to the low-dimensional output space without non-linear activation.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Linear bottleneck projection. Removing non-linear activation (no ReLU/Swish here) prevents manifold collapse in low-dimensional output space.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Ensures compact representation passed across memory cache lines to the next stage.
sublayers.failure_modes: Adding non-linear activation after low-dim projection destroys representation manifolds.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
self.proj_conv = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(expanded_c, out_c, 1, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_c)
)

sublayers.name: DropPath (Stochastic Depth) & Inverted Residual
sublayers.explanation: Randomly drops entire residual paths with linear decay probability during training, regularizing deep subnetworks and preventing co-adaptation.
sublayers.math_breakdown: DropPath Bernoulli mask M ~ Bern(p). Y = X_{in} + (M/p) * X_{proj}. Inverted residual bypass creates direct gradient highways across the 7 stages.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Zero runtime overhead during inference (DropPath disabled, identity addition fused).
sublayers.failure_modes: Static high drop rates cause underfitting; static zero drop rates cause overfitting on CIFAR-100.

sublayers.name: Layer 18: 1x1 Expansion Convolution
sublayers.explanation: Expands final 320 feature channels to 1,280 rich semantic channels before spatial pooling.
sublayers.math_breakdown: 1x1 conv mapping 320 channels to 1280 channels at 4x4 spatial resolution.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Provides high-dimensional linearly separable feature space for the classifier.
sublayers.failure_modes: Direct pooling from 320 channels reduces representational capacity for 100 fine-grained classes.
sublayers.pytorch_code:
self.head_conv = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(320, 1280, 1, bias=False),
    nn.BatchNorm2d(1280),
    nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
)

sublayers.name: Layer 19: Global Average Pooling (GAP)
sublayers.explanation: Collapses 4x4 spatial dimensions into a single 1,280-dimensional feature vector per image, eliminating spatial parameters.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Averages all 16 spatial pixels per channel. Parameter-free operation eliminating millions of dense FC weights (vs traditional AlexNet/VGG FC layers).
sublayers.hardware_notes: Fast reduction kernel with minimal latency and zero weight memory footprint.
sublayers.failure_modes: Using Flatten() instead of GAP causes parameter explosion from 4.03M to >25M weights.

sublayers.name: Layer 20: Classifier Dropout Regularization
sublayers.explanation: Regularizes final 1,280-dimensional feature vector with 20% dropout probability before class logit projection.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Randomly deactivates 20% of features during training to prevent class memorization on CIFAR-100.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Disabled during inference; features pass at full fidelity.
sublayers.failure_modes: Omitting dropout leads to classifier overfitting on subtle CIFAR-100 background artifacts.

sublayers.name: Layer 21: Linear Layer Classifier
sublayers.explanation: Final dense linear projection producing unnormalized class logit scores for all 100 fine-grained CIFAR-100 categories.
sublayers.math_breakdown: Matrix multiplication: (B, 1280) x (1280, 100) -> (B, 100) logits. Parameter count = 1280 * 100 + 100 = 128,100 parameters.
sublayers.hardware_notes: Single GEMM multiplication on output logits.
sublayers.failure_modes: Improper weight initialization causes initial class prediction skew.

pros.claim: Elite Parameter Efficiency (Score: 18.3 vs 14.5 for EfficientNet-B0)
pros.detail: Achieves 26% higher parameter efficiency than EfficientNet-B0 and 32% higher efficiency than MobileNetV3-Large on fine-grained CIFAR-100 classification.

pros.claim: Ultra-Low Deployment Footprint (15.4 MB Storage, 4.03M Params)
pros.detail: Model size is 15.4 MB (66% smaller than ResNet-18 at 44.7 MB and 25% smaller than MobileNetV3-Large at 20.6 MB), ideal for on-device and edge microcontrollers.

pros.claim: 3-Stage Progressive Augmentation (+2.91% Accuracy Gain)
pros.detail: Curriculum-based augmentation schedule stabilizes early training and maximizes generalization, boosting accuracy from 70.8% to 73.71%.

pros.claim: Concentrated 86.6% Parameter Allocation in MBConvSD Blocks
pros.detail: Avoids wasteful parameter bloat in stem and head; focuses 86.6% of weights where depthwise feature extraction and SE channel recalibration occur.

cons.claim: Higher Memory Bandwidth Pressure from Depthwise Kernels on Legacy Hardware
cons.detail: Depthwise convolutions have lower arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte) than dense GEMM, requiring modern mobile DSP/NPU runtimes for maximum speedup.
Specifically architecturalized and tuned for CIFAR-100 resolution; requires stem adaptation for higher resolution ImageNet (224x224) inputs.

reported_benchmarks.comparison_context: 26% higher than EfficientNet-B0 (14.5) and 32% higher than MobileNetV3-Large (13.9)
25% smaller than MobileNetV3 (5.40M) and 66% smaller than ResNet-18 (11.70M)
